params.body:
"Maar hoe kan het ondertussen opnieuw werken?" was the right question, and the answer is a defect.

Every build gives the assets a new hash, and `public/build` lives inside a release. The moment `current` moves, the JS file an already-open page points at is gone. Measured today: release 11:36 served `app-G3PCP_B3.js`, release 11:57 served `app-C35yYWMv.js`, and the first no longer exists under `current`. The browser asks for it, gets a 404, and the screen loses its JavaScript without a word — a switch then does nothing at all, with no message to explain it. A reload fixes it, which is why it "works again by itself".

We deployed twelve times today. At one deploy a week nobody notices; at twelve in a day the operator walks into it repeatedly, and that is what Ilse reported twice.

Two halves, and the second is useless without the first:

- `emptyOutDir: false`, so a build adds to the output directory instead of sweeping it. The manifest is still written fresh, so a new page gets the new hashes and an old page still finds its own. **This needs `public/build` added as a linked (shared) directory in Forge** — that part is outside the repo and is Shane's to set. Until then this flag changes nothing and breaks nothing.
- A guard that says it. The page carries the build it was loaded with and asks `/.well-known/build.json` every quarter of an hour and whenever the tab regains focus. If the running build differs it says so once, with `ui.notify`. It never reloads by itself: the dealer may be halfway through a sheet, and a reload we choose throws that work away.

While in there, a permanently red test turned green. `BuildStamp` claimed in its own docblock to handle a git worktree, and did not: a worktree keeps HEAD in its own gitdir but its refs in the shared one, so the ref was never found and the stamp was null. `BuildStampTest` therefore failed in every worktree run, and today that red line was waved away as known noise all day long. A test that is always red teaches you to ignore tests.

New rule R P1-1.22.
params.title: A deploy does not break an open page
